1: [Psalms of Solomon 1:1-4 — The sinner at the wall]

I cried out to the Lord when I was in distress, to God when sinners assailed me. Suddenly there came the sound of war before my gates, and I said: The Lord will have mercy on me, for I am full of righteousness. And the enemy came over the wall like a thief, and the city did not know him — and the sin of the city had opened the gate before him.
[Psalms of Solomon 2:1-2 — The horses of the enemy]

O Lord, you chose David to be king over Israel, and you swore to him concerning his descendants forever, that his kingdom would never fail before you. But now, because of our sins, sinners have risen against us and driven us out — and the horses of the Gentiles trampled the altar, and the priests of the house carried the vessels into the dust.
2: Do not withhold your hand from us, O God, lest the Gentiles devour us as a lion devours the righteous. Behold, O Lord, and raise up for them their king, the son of David, at the time that you have seen, O God, that he may reign over Israel your servant. And gird him with strength, that he may shatter unrighteous rulers.
[Psalms of Solomon 17:21-25 — The king who shall come]

See, O Lord, and raise up for them their king, the son of David, that he may reign over Israel your servant. And gird him with strength that he may shatter unrighteous rulers, and that he may purge Jerusalem from nations that trample her to destruction. He shall gather a holy people, whom he shall lead in righteousness, and he shall judge the tribes of the people that have been sanctified by the Lord his God.
3: And he himself shall be pure from sin, so that he may rule a great people. He shall rebuke rulers and judge peoples by the word of his mouth. And he shall bless the Lord's people with wisdom and with joy — and he shall be a righteous king, taught by God, over them, and there shall be no unrighteousness in his days, for all shall be holy, and their king shall be the Lord's anointed.

The Lord Himself is king forever and ever. And blessed be the Lord who gives wisdom to the poor of heart. For the wages of the righteous are from the Lord, and He is no respecter of persons — and the meek shall be gathered to Him, and the gathering is His joy, and His joy is the inheritance of the meek.
